title: Scheduler: add KV cache pressure signal + backpressure coordination hooks
author: Sofia Ivanova
release_notes: Internal: scheduler now consumes KV cache pressure signals to coordinate backpressure with allocator/compaction (no external API changes).
description:
Context: KV cache fragmentation/allocator churn under bursty mixes has been causing p95/p99 spikes and occasional allocation failures. The compaction workstream needs an explicit contract between the scheduler and KV cache so we can (a) surface memory pressure early, (b) apply backpressure in a fairness-aware way, and (c) bias scheduling heuristics to avoid making fragmentation worse during bursts.

This PR introduces a lightweight 'cache pressure' signal emitted by the KV cache subsystem and consumed by the scheduler. The signal is used to coordinate backpressure and adjust scheduling heuristics under pressure (without changing request semantics). The default behavior is effectively unchanged when the signal is not present / pressure is low.

Key changes: (1) New runtime interface CachePressureSignal (per device/pool) including: pressure_level (0-3), alloc_fail_recent, fragmentation_ratio_hint (optional), and a recommended action enum (NONE | THROTTLE_PREFILL | THROTTLE_DECODE | SHED_LOW_PRI). (2) Scheduler wiring: the admission controller now consults the signal at the start of each scheduling tick and applies a bounded backoff to new prefills when pressure_level>=2; when pressure_level==3 and alloc_fail_recent==true, we enable temporary shedding for best-effort tier only (SLA-protected tiers are never dropped here; they get queued/backpressured). (3) Heuristic updates: under sustained pressure we reduce the maximum concurrent decode set expansion and avoid selecting new long-context prefills unless the queue would otherwise starve; this reduces worst-case KV growth and allocator churn during bursts. (4) Observability: adds counters and structured logs for (a) pressure_level transitions, (b) scheduler actions taken, and (c) queueing time impact attributed to cache pressure.

Safety/rollout: This is designed to be safe with compaction disabled. The new interfaces default to pressure_level=0. The only behavior change in steady state should be negligible; in stress scenarios, we prefer controlled queuing over allocator-induced tail spikes and OOM. Feature flag hooks are included but not enabled here; follow-up PR (feature flag plumbing) will gate the more aggressive actions if we need a tighter rollout.

Testing: Added unit tests around action selection and tier fairness (no starvation of paid tiers; bounded backoff). Added an integration test in the scheduler sim harness that injects pressure transitions and validates stable throughput and lack of oscillation.

Related: ENG-2846. Pairs with allocator/compaction work in PRs #18431/#18457 and eviction policy v1 #18444. The scheduler contract is documented in-code and will be reflected in ADR-0129.

Notes for reviewers: please focus on (a) fairness invariants, (b) oscillation/feedback loop risk, and (c) whether the pressure signal surface is sufficient for SRE alerting and canary rollback triggers.
commits: scheduler: define CachePressureSignal and action contract
kv-cache: expose pressure snapshot API (no compaction dependency)
admission: apply bounded backoff on prefill under pressure
scheduler: heuristic tweaks to reduce long-context prefill selection under pressure
metrics: counters + structured logs for cache pressure decisions
tests: tier fairness + pressure oscillation guard tests
ci_summary: Buildkite: runtime-linux-gpu (pass), runtime-cpu (pass), unit-tests (pass), scheduler-sim (pass), lint (pass). One flaky scheduler-sim run on 2025-03-06 was rerun and passed.
review_conversation: Noah Patel (architect): The contract looks reasonable. One concern: recommended_action mixes 'what cache wants' and 'what scheduler should do'. Can we ensure scheduler remains the source of truth and cache only provides facts + hints?

Sofia Ivanova (author): Agree. Updated names to make that clearer: CachePressureSnapshot contains facts; SchedulerPressurePolicy produces the action. Cache provides optional hint fields but scheduler can ignore. Also tightened docs in scheduler_cache_pressure_contract.md.
Omar El-Sayed (KV cache): The alloc_fail_recent bit is good. Please ensure it is edge-triggered / decays quickly; otherwise scheduler will stay in 'panic' mode after a single blip.
Sofia Ivanova (author): Implemented a 2s decay window + requires >=2 failures within window to promote to level 3. Added unit test for decay behavior.
Lena Fischer (fairness): For SHED_LOW_PRI, what prevents starvation of best-effort tenants for extended bursts? (We still need some progress or at least bounded queue growth.)

Sofia Ivanova (author): We never shed already-admitted requests; only refuse new admissions for best-effort when pressure_level==3 + alloc_fail_recent. We still allow a small trickle admission (min_admit_qps) to avoid permanent lockout and to reduce oscillations once pressure eases. Added a comment + test asserting min_admit_qps is respected.

Sean Gallagher (SRE): Can you add explicit metrics for 'scheduler_action_taken' with pool/region labels? We need this to correlate canary regressions and build alerting around unexpected pressure actions.

Sofia Ivanova (author): Added runtime_scheduler_cache_pressure_action_total{action,region,pool,tier} and runtime_scheduler_cache_pressure_level{region,pool}. Also included structured log events with action + reason for incident forensics.

Grace Kim (kernels/stream safety): The heuristic change reducing decode set expansion under pressure is fine, but please confirm it doesn't cause head-of-line blocking for short decodes behind long prefills.

Sofia Ivanova (author): The policy only gates new prefills; decode dispatch remains prioritized once admitted. Also added a sim case for mixed short/long where decodes still make progress under pressure.
Julian Moore (scheduler instrumentation): Minor: please keep 'pressure_level' semantics stable (0-3) and document how computed. I see hint fields; want to avoid tight coupling.

Sofia Ivanova (author): Documented as: 0=normal, 1=soft pressure (fragmentation rising), 2=throttle recommended, 3=allocation failures likely/observed. Computation lives in kv_cache_pressure.{h,cc} but scheduler only interprets the discrete level + alloc_fail_recent. Updated docs accordingly.
Noah Patel (architect): Approved after the snapshot/policy split. Nice.
Omar El-Sayed (KV cache): Approved. Decay window change is important.
Sean Gallagher (SRE): Approved. Metrics naming works for dashboards.
